questions.q: In the orchestrator/worker pattern, what is the orchestrator responsible for?
options: Performing every piece of specialized work itself while workers stay idle
Storing embeddings for a vector database
Breaking the overall goal into sub-tasks, delegating them to specialized worker agents, and synthesizing their results
Replacing the need for any worker agents entirely
questions.explain: The orchestrator decomposes, delegates, and assembles — it coordinates the specialized work rather than doing it itself.

questions.q: What is the key distinction between the orchestrator/worker pattern and Lesson 13's planning agent?
options: There is no distinction — they are exactly the same pattern under two different names
Planning agents never use tools, while orchestrators always do
The orchestrator's sub-tasks are determined dynamically based on the specific input, rather than being a fixed, predefined sequence generated once upfront
Orchestrators can only ever delegate to exactly one worker
questions.explain: A planning agent's plan is generated as an ordered sequence; the orchestrator pattern's defining feature is that the breakdown itself varies with what's actually in the input, because it can't be known in advance.

questions.q: In the competitor announcement example, why did the orchestrator spawn a pricing-comparison worker?
options: Because pricing was actually mentioned in that specific announcement — a different announcement without pricing would not spawn that worker
Because every orchestrator run always spawns exactly three workers regardless of input
Because pricing comparison workers are spawned randomly
Because the orchestrator is incapable of ever changing its worker count
questions.explain: The worker breakdown came from what was actually in this input, demonstrating the dynamic (not fixed) decomposition that defines the pattern.

questions.q: How does the orchestrator/worker pattern relate to the Claude Agent SDK's subagents from Lesson 14?
options: They are unrelated — subagents cannot be used to implement this pattern
Subagents replace the need for an orchestrator entirely, with no coordinating agent required
Orchestrator/worker only applies to agents built without the Claude Agent SDK

Orchestrator/worker is the pattern name for organizing work this way, and subagents are the SDK's concrete mechanism for implementing it — the orchestrator role is what a main agent plays when invoking subagents
questions.explain: A main agent invoking subagents for focused subtasks is literally playing the orchestrator role, with each subagent acting as a worker running in its own separate context.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what signal suggests reaching for the orchestrator pattern rather than a fixed plan?
options: The task simply has more than one step in total
The number and shape of needed sub-tasks genuinely depends on what's in the specific request, and can't be known in advance
The task never requires more than a single tool call
The orchestrator pattern should be used for every task regardless of its structure
questions.explain: Having multiple steps alone doesn't require this pattern — Lesson 13's planning agent already handles that. The orchestrator pattern specifically fits when the breakdown itself must be discovered per-input.
